**Reeves announces open banking governance overhaul in Mansion House reforms**

*The UK chancellor has set out changes to the Open Banking Future Entity and the long-term regulatory framework, moving open banking's governance closer to formal regulatory oversight.*

Rachel Reeves, the UK chancellor, used her Mansion House speech on July 16 to announce a package of reforms to the UK's open banking framework. The changes address the governance of the Open Banking Future Entity and signal the direction of the long-term regulatory settlement, including how variable recurring payments and new data-sharing use cases will be supervised.

The announcements sit alongside HM Treasury's broader consultation on modernising payment services regulation, published the same day with a response deadline of October 6. That consultation, which also covers stablecoins and the planned absorption of the Payment Systems Regulator into the FCA, forms part of the government's National Payments Vision. It asks whether adjustments are needed to support emerging open banking payment and data use cases.

Taken together, the Mansion House speech and the HMT consultation represent the most concrete articulation yet of how the UK government intends to bridge the gap between the CMA's original open banking mandate and the broader open finance agenda. For firms building on open banking rails, the regulatory framework that emerges from this consultation will shape what products are commercially viable and on what terms.

*Sources: [UK Chancellor makes announcements on 'evolution' of Open Banking in Mansion House reforms](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/uk-chancellor-makes-announcements-on-evolution-of-open-banking-in-mansion-house-reforms/) — Openbankingexpo | [HM Treasury consults on a future-proof framework for payments, stablecoins and Open Banking](https://www.lewissilkin.com/insights/2026/07/16/hm-treasury-consults-on-a-future-proof-framework-for-payments-stablecoins-and-op-102nc2h) — Lewissilkin | [HMT consults on Modernising Payment Services Regulation](https://www.regulationtomorrow.com/2026/07/hmt-consults-on-modernising-payment-services-regulation/) — Regulationtomorrow*
stories.edited:
**Reeves announces Mansion House reforms to accelerate UK open banking**

*The chancellor's speech signals structural changes to the Open Banking Future Entity and the long-term regulatory framework, moving open banking closer to open finance.*

Rachel Reeves, the UK chancellor, used her Mansion House speech on July 16 to announce a package of reforms aimed at the next phase of open banking. The measures address the governance of the Open Banking Future Entity and set out a longer-term regulatory pathway intended to support new payment and data-sharing use cases, including variable recurring payments.

The announcements sit within the government's broader National Payments Vision and follow Reeves's July 14 commitment to an open finance push focused on SME lending. Taken together, the two interventions mark a shift from aspiration to structural detail, with the Future Entity's mandate and regulatory underpinning now under active redesign rather than industry self-governance.

For payments firms and banks, the practical question is how quickly the updated framework translates into new commercial permissions. The speech acknowledged that adjustments may be needed to support emerging open banking payment and data use cases, but specifics on timelines and scope remain subject to the parallel HMT consultation.

*Sources: [UK Chancellor makes announcements on 'evolution' of Open Banking in Mansion House reforms](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/uk-chancellor-makes-announcements-on-evolution-of-open-banking-in-mansion-house-reforms/) — Openbankingexpo*

**Stripe and Advent table $53 billion joint bid to acquire PayPal**

*A joint approach by Stripe and Advent International for PayPal would, if completed, reshape the competitive landscape for online payments and merchant acquiring globally.*

Stripe and Advent International, the private equity firm, have tabled a joint bid to acquire PayPal for approximately $53 billion, according to reports on July 16. The approach comes as PayPal's new leadership has been restructuring the business, having recently shut down its venture capital arm and refocused on core payment processing.

A deal of this scale would consolidate two of the largest independent online payment platforms under common ownership. Stripe's strength in developer-led merchant acquiring and PayPal's consumer wallet and checkout presence are largely complementary, though the overlap in online merchant payments would draw regulatory scrutiny in multiple jurisdictions. Advent's involvement suggests the financial structure may involve significant leverage and a potential future re-listing or break-up.

For European payments specifically, the combination would create a platform with deep reach across both account-to-account and card-based rails. PayPal recently joined the European Payments Council and has been expanding its BNPL offering in the UK, while Stripe has built partnerships with banks such as Lloyds and with government clients. Whether the bid progresses to a formal offer remains uncertain, but the strategic logic — and the antitrust complexity — will define industry discussion for months.

*Sources: [The future of consumer payments: Cards, Pay by Bank & the evolution of the multi-rail bank](https://www.finextra.com/event-info/624/the-future-of-consumer-payments-cards-pay-by-bank--the-evolution-of-the-multi-rail-bank?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**HM Treasury consults on modernising UK payments, stablecoins and open banking rules**

*A wide-ranging consultation proposes a future-proof regulatory framework covering payment services, stablecoins and open banking, with responses due by October 6.*

HM Treasury has opened a consultation on modernising the UK's payments regulation, covering payment services, stablecoins and open banking within a single framework. The consultation, published on July 14, forms part of the National Payments Vision and follows the planned absorption of the Payment Systems Regulator into the FCA.

The scope is broad. HMT is considering whether the existing regulatory perimeter needs adjusting to accommodate new open banking payment and data use cases, alongside questions about stablecoin oversight and broader payment services rules. The FCA, PSR and Bank of England are all listed as co-engaged regulators.

Responses are due by October 6. For the industry, this is the formal mechanism through which the Mansion House commitments will take concrete regulatory shape. Firms with positions on variable recurring payments, open banking licensing or stablecoin treatment will need to engage directly.

*Sources: [HM Treasury consults on a future-proof framework for payments, stablecoins and Open Banking](https://www.lewissilkin.com/insights/2026/07/16/hm-treasury-consults-on-a-future-proof-framework-for-payments-stablecoins-and-op-102nc2h) — Lewissilkin | [HMT consults on Modernising Payment Services Regulation](https://www.regulationtomorrow.com/2026/07/hmt-consults-on-modernising-payment-services-regulation/) — Regulationtomorrow | [HMT consults on Modernising Payment Services Regulation](https://www.regulationtomorrow.com/2026/07/hmt-consults-on-modernising-payment-services-regulation/) — Regulationtomorrow | [HMT consults on Modernising Payment Services Regulation](https://www.regulationtomorrow.com/2026/07/hmt-consults-on-modernising-payment-services-regulation/) — Regulationtomorrow*

**Thredd joins Visa's agentic payments programme across Europe**

*The issuer processor's participation in Visa's Agentic Ready programme lets European card issuers support AI agent-initiated payments without rebuilding existing infrastructure.*

Thredd, the issuer processing platform, announced on July 16 that it is joining Visa's Agentic Ready programme. The integration enables issuers across Europe that process through Thredd to participate in agent-initiated payments — transactions where an AI agent acts on a consumer's behalf — without needing to overhaul their payments stack.

Agentic payments have moved rapidly from concept to early production in 2026. Visa launched its own agentic payments capability in Europe in early July, and competitors such as Mastercard and ING completed Europe's first agentic payment in June. The infrastructure layer is now catching up: processor-level support from firms such as Thredd means the capability can scale beyond pilot banks to a broader issuer base.

For the European market, the question is shifting from whether agentic payments will arrive to how quickly the supporting infrastructure — authorisation, fraud controls, consent management — can be standardised. Thredd's move suggests that established processors see enough near-term demand to invest in readiness now, rather than waiting for regulatory frameworks to settle.

*Sources: [Thredd joins Visa's Agentic Ready programme](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110439/thredd-joins-visas-agentic-ready-programme?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Stripe and Advent table joint bid to acquire PayPal for $53 billion**

*A potential deal would reshape the European and global payments landscape by combining Stripe's merchant platform with PayPal's consumer wallet and checkout network.*

Stripe and private equity firm Advent International have tabled a joint bid to acquire PayPal in a deal valued at approximately $53 billion. The approach, first reported on July 16, would represent one of the largest transactions in payments history.

PayPal has been restructuring under CEO Alex Chriss, who took over in September 2023. The company shut down its venture capital arm in June and has been refocusing on core payment processing and checkout. A combination with Stripe would unite two of the largest online payment processors, with significant overlap in merchant acquiring and divergent strengths in consumer wallets and developer infrastructure.

The deal's outcome is far from assured — regulatory review across multiple jurisdictions, including the EU and UK, would be extensive given the combined market share in online payments. For European payments firms, the prospect of a merged Stripe-PayPal entity raises competitive questions for acquirers, pay-by-bank providers and alternative checkout networks alike.

*Sources: [UK Chancellor makes announcements on 'evolution' of Open Banking in Mansion House reforms](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/uk-chancellor-makes-announcements-on-evolution-of-open-banking-in-mansion-house-reforms/) — Openbankingexpo*

**Linux Foundation rallies 40 firms behind internet-native payments protocol**

*The x402 protocol, backed by a coalition of finance and technology companies, aims to embed payment capability directly into internet infrastructure — a potentially significant shift in how machines and AI agents settle transactions online.*

The Linux Foundation has assembled 40 finance and technology firms to support x402, a protocol designed to enable payments to be sent natively over the internet. The initiative, reported on July 16, repurposes the long-dormant HTTP 402 "Payment Required" status code as the basis for a standardised machine-to-machine payment layer.

The protocol is designed for scenarios where automated systems — including AI agents — need to pay for access to web content, APIs or services without human intervention. Unlike existing payment integrations, which rely on merchant-specific checkout flows, x402 would function as a transport-layer standard, making payment a built-in capability of web requests rather than an application bolted on top.

The breadth of the coalition and the Linux Foundation's involvement lend the initiative more credibility than a typical startup protocol proposal. If x402 gains adoption, it could become foundational infrastructure for agentic commerce, where AI agents transact autonomously. For European payment providers, it raises questions about which rails — card, account-to-account, stablecoin — will plug into the protocol layer and capture this emerging transaction flow.

*Sources: [Finance and tech firms unite around Internet payments protocol x402](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48105/finance-and-tech-firms-unite-around-internet-payments-protocol-x402?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Thredd joins Visa's agentic payments programme for European issuers**

*The issuer processor's participation in Visa's Agentic Ready programme gives European card issuers a route into agent-initiated payments without rebuilding their infrastructure.*

Thredd, the issuer processing platform, has joined Visa's Agentic Ready programme, enabling its issuer clients across Europe to support payments initiated by AI agents. The arrangement lets issuers participate in the emerging agentic commerce layer without replacing existing payment infrastructure.

Agentic payments — where AI agents initiate and authorise transactions on behalf of consumers or businesses — have moved rapidly from concept to early production in 2026. Visa launched its own agentic payments capabilities in Europe on July 2, and Mastercard, ING and Worldline completed Europe's first agentic payment in early June. Thredd's integration extends this capability to a wider set of European issuers through a processing layer rather than direct scheme membership.

The announcement is one of a growing number of infrastructure-level moves positioning European payment firms for agentic commerce. The pace of programme enrolments suggests the industry expects agent-initiated transactions to reach meaningful volume sooner than many initially predicted.

*Sources: [Thredd joins Visa's Agentic Ready programme](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110439/thredd-joins-visas-agentic-ready-programme?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.edited:
**Linux Foundation rallies 40 firms behind internet-native payments protocol x402**

*The initiative to standardise machine-to-machine payments over the internet draws backing from finance and technology companies, signalling growing demand for a protocol-level payment layer.*

The Linux Foundation has assembled 40 finance and technology firms behind x402, an open protocol designed to enable payments to be sent natively over the internet. The protocol targets machine-to-machine and automated payment flows, areas where existing card and bank transfer rails were not designed to operate.

The x402 protocol — named after the HTTP 402 "Payment Required" status code that has existed since the early web but was never widely implemented — aims to create a standardised way for software to request and send payments as part of web interactions. The coalition's breadth, spanning finance and technology, suggests the initiative is positioning itself as infrastructure rather than a single-vendor product.

For the European payments industry, x402 intersects with live debates around agentic commerce, open banking payment initiation and the role of stablecoins as settlement instruments. Whether the protocol gains traction depends on whether it can offer something that existing payment APIs and account-to-account rails cannot — namely, a universal, protocol-level payment primitive that works across schemes and jurisdictions.

*Sources: [Finance and tech firms unite around Internet payments protocol x402](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48105/finance-and-tech-firms-unite-around-internet-payments-protocol-x402?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
